source.probe: Word probe from meiryo.ttc: Latin Verdana-derived at 0.9705x (bold 0.948x), kana via the bundled GenOffice UI Kana JP faces

note:
Meiryo / Meiryo UI (Word-private on macOS; Word renders them real, probe
2026-09-03 from Word's meiryo.ttc). Meiryo UI kana are proportional
(text-weighted mean 0.769em, bold 0.820em), U+30FC 0.816/0.882em,
ideographic space and 、。 0.664em, corner/angle brackets and ・ 0.5em, at
full glyph height; kanji and （）：；！？ stay 1em and fall through to the
chain. The bundled GenOffice UI Kana JP faces (tools/build-meiryo-ui-kana-
font.py: Noto Sans JP outlines condensed horizontally to Meiryo UI's exact
per-glyph advances) carry those ranges — a size-adjust alias would shrink
the height too and leave kana at ~77% next to full-size kanji. Latin in
both cuts is Verdana-derived at 0.9705x (bold 0.948x); Hiragino W3/W6
backstops hosts without Verdana. Installed Meiryo (Windows) still precedes
these aliases in the chain.
